What is Coral Reef?
“The corals that live in reef habitats are protected by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List,” says Dr. Maria Kowalski. “In addition to its role as a nursery area, it protects the health of tropical reef ecosystems. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), in collaboration with the United States Department of Energy (DOE), NOAA, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), spearheaded this effort.”
Why Is Coral Reef Important?
Dr. Maria Kowalski points out that reefs are important because they provide habitat for many species, including fish, turtles, and even sharks. Coral reefs also support a diverse range of marine life, such as corals, sponges, corals, and corals-like animals such as corals. Because of these characteristics, coral reefs can be home to hundreds of different species of fish and other wildlife.
